definition.rules:
### Project tempo (and often key) is global

The tempo map is a project-level property. Recorded audio is fitted to it (by warping or by performance), notes and patterns are defined against it, and changing it re-times the whole project. Key-aware products extend the same logic to musical key.

### Editing is non-destructive by default

Clips and regions reference the original recorded material; edits are instructions, not rewrites. The underlying take survives until the user explicitly consolidates or bounces.

### Track type constrains content

Audio tracks hold recordings; instrument tracks hold notes played by devices. The two do not mix freely within one track — converting between them is an explicit operation (audio-to-MIDI, rendering notes to audio).

### The deliverable is audio

A song is finished when it leaves the application as an audio file — full mix or stems. Project files are working documents, not deliverables; they also bind the user to the product, which is why export breadth matters.

### Single-operator tool with file-based collaboration

There is no organizational permission model. Sharing happens by exporting audio/stems, exchanging project files (with their referenced assets), or — in cloud variants — by publishing. A project's referenced files must travel with it or be collected into it, or it will not open correctly elsewhere.

### Edition and tier gating shape the same core

Products ship in editions or tiers that gate capabilities — most notably, some gate audio recording itself behind higher editions, and entry tiers cap track counts or library size. The gating changes what a given installation can do, not what the Type is.
definition.rules_zh:
### 项目速度（通常还有调性）是全局的

速度图是项目级属性。录制的音频被适配到它（通过变形或表演），音符和节奏型相对于它定义，更改它重新计时整个项目。调性感知的产品将相同逻辑扩展到音乐调性。

### 编辑默认是非破坏性的

片段和区域引用原始录制素材；编辑是指令，而非重写。底层录音在用户明确合并或弹跳之前依然存在。

### 轨道类型限制内容

音频轨道承载录音；乐器轨道承载由设备演奏的音符。两者不在一个轨道内自由混合——在它们之间转换是明确的操作（音频到MIDI，将音符渲染为音频）。

### 交付物是音频

当歌曲以音频文件形式离开应用程序时——完整混音或分轨——歌曲就完成了。项目文件是工作文档，而非交付物；它们还将用户绑定到产品，这就是为什么导出广度很重要。

### 单操作员工具，基于文件的协作

没有组织权限模型。共享通过导出音频/分轨、交换项目文件（及其引用的资源）或——在云端变体中——通过发布发生。项目的引用文件必须随其移动或被收集到其中，否则它将在其他地方无法正确打开。

### 版本和层级门控塑造相同的核心

产品以版本或层级发布，门控能力——最值得注意的是，一些将音频录制本身门控在更高版本之后，入门层级限制轨道数量或库大小。门控改变给定安装能做什么，而非改变类型是什么。

definition.name: Virtual Recording Studio
definition.overview:
A **Virtual Recording Studio** is an application that provides a music recording studio on a computer: the user records sound, creates musical material with built-in instruments, arranges it into tracks on a shared timeline, mixes the tracks into a unified whole, and renders the finished song as audio.

The products sold and described under this name are the ones the music industry calls **digital audio workstations (DAWs)**. Vendors use the two vocabularies interchangeably for the same products — one vendor describes its product as "DAW software" and, on the same page, as "a single virtual studio package"; another's product page carries a press quote that apposes the two in one sentence ("a fully-fledged music studio inside your computer — n-Track is a digital audio workstation"); a third names its mixing toolset "online DAW features" while calling the workspace "the studio". The framing spans the whole family, from free consumer products ("a fully equipped music creation studio right inside your Mac") to professional ones ("Turn your Mac into a full recording studio"). This document describes that product family from the studio framing — the studio the computer becomes; the Digital Audio Workstation document describes the same family from the workstation framing, and is the canonical name per a completed joint review of the directory entries.

The defining core is small:

```text
Music project (persistent; survives save/open)
└── Tracks carrying user-created musical material (recorded audio and/or authored notes/patterns)
    └── Mixing (per-track level/pan/processing combined into a unified output)
        └── Rendered deliverable (the finished track leaves as audio)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the "studio in your computer" pitch — the bundled instruments, the loop libraries, the amp simulators, the AI stem separation, the cloud collaboration — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product a virtual recording studio. A rack-based product from 1994, a cross-platform product first released in the 1990s, and a browser studio all satisfy the same core without any of those additions.

When the primary job is editing an existing recording rather than building a song, the product is an Audio Editor; when it narrows to rhythm-anchored pattern composition, a Beat-making Application; when it is performing finished tracks, DJ Software.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**虚拟录音棚**是一种在计算机上提供音乐录音棚功能的应用程序：用户录制声音，使用内置乐器创作音乐素材，将其编排到共享时间线上的音轨中，将音轨混音为一个统一的整体，并将完成的歌曲渲染为音频。

在此名称下销售和描述的产品，是音乐产业所称的**数字音频工作站（DAW）**。供应商对相同产品互换使用这两套词汇——一家供应商将其产品描述为“DAW软件”，并在同一页面上描述为“单一虚拟工作室套件”；另一家供应商的产品页面引用了一段新闻引语，将两者并置于一句话中（“您电脑内的全功能音乐工作室——n-Track 是一个数字音频工作站”）；第三家将其混音工具集命名为“在线 DAW 功能”，同时称工作区为“工作室”。这种定位涵盖了整个产品家族，从免费消费级产品（“您 Mac 内部配备齐全的音乐创作工作室”）到专业级产品（“将您的 Mac 变成完整的录音棚”）。本文档从工作室定位描述该产品家族——计算机变成的那个工作室；数字音频工作站文档从工作站定位描述同一家族，并且根据已完成的目录条目联合审查，这是规范名称。

定义性核心很小：

```text
音乐项目（持久化；在保存/打开后依然存在）
└── 承载用户创作音乐素材的音轨（录制音频和/或创作的音符/模式）
     └── 混音（每轨电平/声像/处理组合为统一输出）
         └── 渲染交付物（完成的音轨以音频形式输出）
```

通常与“您电脑中的工作室”宣传相关联的一切——捆绑乐器、循环库、放大器模拟器、AI 人声分离、云协作——在当前产品中很普遍，但这并非使产品成为虚拟录音棚的原因。一款 1994 年的机架式产品、一款 1990 年代首次发布的跨平台产品，以及一款浏览器工作室，均满足相同核心，而不具备任何上述附加功能。

当主要工作是编辑现有录音而非构建歌曲时，该产品是音频编辑器；当它缩小到以节奏为锚点的模式作曲时，是节拍制作应用；当它播放完成的音轨时，是 DJ 软件。
definition.dc:
```text
Music project
└── Tracks (parallel, over one shared timeline)
    └── User-created musical material
        ├── recorded audio (vocals, instruments, captured sound)
        └── authored notes/patterns (played or drawn, played by instruments)
    └── Mixing (level, pan, processing per track → one combined output)
        └── Rendered deliverable (finished track as audio)
```

Four properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a virtual recording studio:

- **Persistent music project** — the song lives in a document that survives save/open and accumulates work over days or months. Without persistence it is a jam tool; without multitrack and a shared timeline it is an audio editor.
- **User-created musical material in tracks** — the song is *built* inside the application. The material is either recorded sound or authored notes/patterns; at least one authoring path must exist. Without this, the product is a player or editor for material that already exists.
- **Mixing** — the tracks are combined: per-track level, pan, and processing resolve into one output. Without this, the product is a recorder.
- **Rendered deliverable** — the finished track leaves the application as audio (a full mix, or stems for further work). Without this, it is not a production tool.

Neither recording nor note-authoring is individually required — products exist that gate audio recording behind higher editions, and pattern-only environments have carried the family — but at least one path for creating material in the application is.
definition.dc_zh:
音乐项目
└── 轨道（并行，在一个共享时间线上）
    └── 用户创建的音乐素材
        ├── 录制的音频（人声、乐器、捕获的声音）
        └── 创作的音符/模式（演奏或绘制，由乐器演奏）
    └── 混音（音量、声像、每轨道处理 → 一个组合输出）
        └── 渲染的交付物（完成的音轨作为音频）
definition.rules:
### Project tempo (and often key) is global

The tempo map is a project-level property. Recorded audio is fitted to it, notes and patterns are defined against it, and changing it re-times the whole project.

### Editing is non-destructive by default

Clips and regions reference the original recorded material; edits are instructions, not rewrites. The underlying take survives until the user explicitly consolidates or bounces.

### Track type constrains content

Audio tracks hold recordings; instrument tracks hold notes played by devices. Converting between them is an explicit operation (audio-to-MIDI, rendering notes to audio).

### The deliverable is audio

A song is finished when it leaves the application as an audio file. Project files are working documents, not deliverables; they also bind the user to the product, which is why export breadth matters.

### Single-operator tool with file-based collaboration — unless it is a cloud variant

There is no organizational permission model. Sharing happens by exporting audio/stems or exchanging project files. Cloud variants add real-time multi-user editing of shared projects with auto-save — the collaboration model changes, the production model does not.

### Edition and tier gating shape the same core

Products ship in editions or plans that gate capabilities — bundled content size, effects and instruments, advanced tools, and in some products audio recording itself. The gating changes what a given installation can do, not what the Type is.
definition.rules_zh:
### 项目速度（通常还有调性）是全局的

速度图是项目级属性。录制音频被适配到它，音符和模式针对它定义，更改它重新计时整个项目。

### 编辑默认是非破坏性的

片段和区域引用原始录制素材；编辑是指令，而非重写。底层录音在用户明确合并或弹回之前依然存在。

### 音轨类型限制内容

音频音轨承载录音；乐器音轨承载由设备演奏的音符。在它们之间转换是明确操作（音频转 MIDI，将音符渲染为音频）。

### 交付物是音频

当歌曲以音频文件形式离开应用程序时，它即完成。项目文件是工作文档，而非交付物；它们还将用户绑定到产品，这就是为什么导出广度很重要。

### 单操作员工具，基于文件的协作——除非它是云变体

没有组织权限模型。分享通过导出音频/分轨或交换项目文件发生。云变体添加对共享项目的实时多用户编辑和自动保存——协作模型改变，生产模型不变。

### 版本和层级门控塑造相同核心

产品以版本或计划发布，门控能力——捆绑内容大小、效果和乐器、高级工具，在某些产品中还有音频录制本身。门控改变给定安装能做什么，而非改变类型是什么。

definition.name: Music Notation Editor
definition.overview:
A **Music Notation Editor** is an authoring application for creating and revising music as **notated scores**: persistent documents whose content is music expressed in musical semantics — pitches with durations, rests, voices, meter, and performance markings — and which the software renders as conventional staff notation.

The defining core is small:

```text
Score (persistent document of one piece of music)
└── music-semantic editing (content changed as musical meaning, validity maintained)
    └── rendering as conventional staff notation (engraved output that follows the content)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — instrument/staff structure, playback, automatic layout, parts generation, MusicXML interchange, cloud collaboration, education packaging, scanning — is standard capability or variant, not definition. A hand-engraved manuscript satisfies the same core with no software at all; print-era engraving programs satisfy it without playback or cloud features. When the deliverable shifts from the notated score to a produced audio mix, the product has moved into digital audio workstation territory; when authoring is removed and only consumption remains, it becomes a sheet music reader.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**乐谱记谱编辑器**是一种用于创建和修订音乐**记谱总谱**的编写应用程序：这些是持久化的文档，其内容是以音乐语义表达的音乐——具有时值的音高、休止符、声部、拍号以及演奏标记——软件将其渲染为传统的五线谱记谱。

其定义性的核心很小：

```text
总谱（单首音乐的持久化文档）
└── 音乐语义编辑（内容作为音乐意义被更改，有效性得以维持）
     └── 渲染为传统五线谱记谱（遵循内容的印刷输出）
```

通常与该类别相关联的其他所有内容——乐器/谱表结构、回放、自动排版、分谱生成、MusicXML 交换、云端协作、教育打包、扫描——都是标准功能或变体，而非定义。一份手工雕刻的手稿在没有软件的情况下也能满足同样的核心；印刷时代的雕刻程序在没有回放或云端功能的情况下也能满足它。当交付物从记谱总谱转变为制作好的音频混音时，该产品已进入数字音频工作站领域；当编写被移除且仅保留消费时，它就变成了乐谱阅读器。
definition.dc: The central object is the **score**: a persistent, named, saveable document whose content is one piece of music held as notation. The score is the system of record — everything else (layout, parts, playback, exports) is derived from it.
definition.dc_zh: 核心对象是**乐谱**：一个持久的、命名的、可保存的文档，其内容是以记谱形式保存的一首音乐作品。乐谱是系统的记录本——所有其他内容（布局、声部、播放、导出）都由此派生。
definition.rules:
- **Musical validity is maintained by the software.** Durations must add up within measures; the editor places events at valid rhythmic positions, corrects or flags impossible rhythms, and keeps meter consistent. The user composes; the software guarantees notational coherence.
- **Content and rendering are separated.** Moving or resizing a symbol changes the *layout*, not the music; changing a pitch re-renders the layout around it. Automatic layout reflows as content changes — manual placement is an override, not the source of truth.
- **Notation conventions are enforced.** The software renders per established engraving practice (stem directions, beam grouping, symbol placement) rather than offering free graphic placement; fine control exists but operates on musical objects.
- **Key signature and accidental semantics.** Pitches are interpreted against the prevailing key signature; accidentals alter pitches within defined scopes. Transposing instruments display in their own transposition while the score can be viewed in concert pitch.
- **Parts follow the score.** Where parts are generated, they remain linked: an edit in the master score propagates to the part; part-specific layout is local.
- **Interchange has fidelity tiers.** Semantic formats (MusicXML, MIDI) carry the music to other tools — with some fidelity loss in complex notation; PDF/audio are fixed renderings that cannot be re-edited as notation.
- **Versions and history.** Editing is reversible (undo; and in cloud products, restore-to-earlier-version history).
definition.rules_zh:
- **音乐有效性由软件维持。** 时值必须在小节内相加；编辑器将事件放置在有效的节奏位置，纠正或标记不可能的节奏，并保持拍号一致。用户进行创作；软件保证记谱的连贯性。
- **内容与渲染分离。** 移动或调整符号大小改变的是*排版*，而非音乐；改变音高会围绕它重新渲染排版。自动排版随内容变化而重排——手动放置是覆盖，而非真实来源。
- **强制记谱惯例。** 软件根据既定的雕刻实践（符干方向、符杠分组、符号放置）进行渲染，而不是提供自由的图形放置；精细控制存在，但作用于音乐对象。
- **调号与变音记号语义。** 音高根据当前调号进行解释；变音记号在定义的范围内改变音高。移调乐器以其自身的移调显示，而总谱可以以合奏音高查看。
- **分谱跟随总谱。** 在生成分谱的地方，它们保持链接：总谱中的编辑传播到分谱；特定于分谱的排版是局部的。
- **交换具有保真度层级。** 语义格式（MusicXML, MIDI）将音乐携带到其他工具——在复杂记谱中会有一些保真度损失；PDF/音频是固定的渲染，不能作为记谱重新编辑。
- **版本与历史。** 编辑是可逆的（撤销；以及在云端产品中，恢复到早期版本的历史）。

definition.name: Sheet Music Reader
definition.overview:
A **Sheet Music Reader** is a performer-facing application for reading notated music: it holds scores as a persistent, organized library, presents them on screen for music-reading with direct control of the reading state — page position, page turning, display arrangement — and operates on those existing scores through marking up, playing along, and organizing them for practice and performance.

The defining structure is small:

```text
The score (a displayable document of one piece of notated music)
└── The score-reading surface (the music presented for reading,
    organized around its own pagination)
    └── The performer's library (collected scores, organized
        and retrieved for practice and performance)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — annotation ink, hands-free page turning, playback, metronomes and practice tools, cloud sync, ensemble collaboration, scanning, subscription catalogs — is a standard capability or variant built on that core, not what makes the product a sheet music reader. The proof is historical as well as structural: a music binder on a stand, with a pencil and a setlist sheet tucked inside the cover, is the same application in paper form.

The reader is a consumption application. It operates on scores that already exist — imported, scanned, purchased, or drawn from a catalog — rather than authoring the notation itself. When that relationship flips and creating or editing the music becomes the point, the product has moved into music notation editor territory.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**乐谱阅读器**是面向演奏者的应用，用于阅读记谱音乐：它将乐谱作为持久化、有条理的库进行存储，在屏幕上呈现乐谱以供阅读，并直接控制阅读状态——页面位置、翻页、显示布局——并通过标记、跟奏以及为练习和演出组织乐谱来操作这些现有乐谱。

其定义性结构很小：

```text
乐谱（一件记谱音乐的可显示文档）
└── 乐谱阅读界面（为阅读而呈现的音乐，
    围绕其自身的分页进行组织）
     └── 演奏者的库（收集的乐谱，
        为练习和演出进行组织和检索）
```

通常与该类别相关联的其他所有内容——注释墨水、免提翻页、播放、节拍器和练习工具、云同步、合奏协作、扫描、订阅目录——都是基于该核心构建的标准功能或变体，而非使产品成为乐谱阅读器的原因。证明既是历史的也是结构性的：一个放在支架上的乐谱夹，里面夹着一支铅笔和一张曲目单，就是该应用的纸质形式。

阅读器是一种消费型应用。它操作的是已经存在的乐谱——导入的、扫描的、购买的或从目录中获取的——而不是创作记谱本身。当这种关系反转，创作或编辑音乐成为重点时，该产品就进入了乐谱记谱编辑器的领域。
definition.dc:
Three structures, each load-bearing:

**The score as the unit of record.** A persistent, identified, displayable document of one piece of notated music, held by the application. It carries an identity and typically metadata (composer, genre, instrumentation, key) and is the object to which everything else attaches — annotations, bookmarks, setlist membership, audio. It is *held*, not ephemeral: scores accumulate in the application across sessions and years. Realizations vary: a PDF file, a set of scanned page images, a converted interactive score, or an edition delivered from a licensed catalog. The document form is an implementation choice; the held, displayable, per-piece record is the invariant.

**The score-reading surface.** The score displayed for human music-reading, organized around the music's own pagination and structure, with direct control of the reading state: what page is showing, how pages turn, how pages are arranged on screen (single page, two-page spread, half-page, scrolling), and how the notation fills the display (zoom, cropping, reflow for small screens). This surface is optimized for a reader whose eyes stay on the music and whose hands are usually elsewhere — which is why page turning is a first-class behavior rather than a scrolled afterthought.

**The performer's library.** The collected scores of a person or an ensemble, stored, organized, and retrieved for use. Organization is typically metadata-driven — composer, genre, instrument, occasion — with search and filtering designed to find any piece in seconds, and, for performance contexts, ordered programs of pieces (setlists) that page through a whole evening's music seamlessly. Separate libraries for separate bands or roles are a common pattern. Without the library, the reader is a one-off viewer; without the reading surface, it is a catalog; without the score, neither exists.
definition.dc_zh:
三个结构，每个都承重：

**乐谱作为记录单位。** 一个持久的、已识别的、可显示的单一记谱音乐作品文档，由应用程序持有。它携带身份和通常元数据（作曲家、体裁、乐器、调），并且是其他所有内容附加的对象——注释、书签、曲目列表成员身份、音频。它是*被持有*的，不是短暂的：乐谱在应用程序中跨会话和年份累积。实现方式多样：PDF文件、一组扫描页面图像、转换的交互式乐谱，或从授权目录交付的版本。文档形式是实现选择；被持有的、可显示的、每作品记录是不变的。

**乐谱阅读界面。** 为人类音乐阅读而显示的乐谱，围绕音乐自身的分页和结构组织，直接控制阅读状态：显示哪一页、页面如何翻页、页面在屏幕上如何排列（单页、双页展开、半页、滚动），以及记谱如何填充显示（缩放、裁剪、为小屏幕重排）。此界面为眼睛停留在音乐上且手通常在别处的读者优化——这就是为什么翻页是一等行为，而不是滚动后的想法。

**表演者的库。** 一个人或一个团体的收集乐谱，存储、组织和可检索。
definition.rules:
- **Annotations are a layer, not a revision.** Marking a score does not change the notation; the score document stays intact beneath the marks. Duplicates of the same score carry independent annotations — the mechanism that lets one musician keep different markings for different gigs, or an ensemble distribute one clean score while everyone marks it up privately.
- **Reading state is reachable hands-free.** Because the performer's hands are occupied, mature products provide at least one non-touch path through the score loop — pedal, MIDI, gesture, automatic scroll, or device sync. Touch remains the fallback, not the only path.
- **Page-turn responsiveness is treated as a hard requirement.** Products engineer caching and rendering so that a page turn never stalls a performance. A reader that hesitates at page boundaries fails at its central use.
- **The library replaces the file system.** Scores are found through metadata, categories, and search rather than by remembering where a file was saved; products explicitly organize for retrieval speed ("find any song in seconds") over storage structure.
- **Offline first, cloud second.** Scores held on the device read without a connection; cloud sync, shared projects, and catalog access require one. A performer cannot depend on venue Wi-Fi, so the held score is the contract.
- **Sync preserves per-musician markings.** When libraries or projects are distributed across an ensemble, each musician's annotations survive the merge rather than being overwritten — ensemble marking is personal even on shared music.
- **Notation-aware operations act on the document, not as authoring.** Transposition, section navigation, or MusicXML/MIDI export in such products derive from the stored (or converted) score; the reader's center of gravity remains presenting and operating on existing music. Where changing the notation itself becomes the primary activity, the product has crossed into notation-editor territory.
definition.rules_zh:
- **注释是一层，而非修订。** 标记乐谱不会改变记谱；乐谱文档在标记之下保持完整。同一乐谱的副本携带独立的注释——这是让一位音乐家为不同演出保留不同标记，或让合奏分发一份干净乐谱而每个人私下标记的机制。
- **阅读状态可免提到达。** 因为演奏者的双手被占用，成熟产品提供至少一条非触摸路径通过乐谱循环——踏板、MIDI、手势、自动滚动或设备同步。触摸仍是后备，而非唯一路径。
- **翻页响应性被视为硬性要求。** 产品工程化缓存和渲染，使翻页永不阻碍演出。在页面边界犹豫的阅读器在其核心用途上失败。
- **库取代文件系统。** 乐谱通过元数据、类别和搜索找到，而非靠记住文件保存位置；产品明确为检索速度（“几秒内找到任何歌曲”）而非存储结构进行组织。
- **离线优先，云端其次。** 设备上的乐谱无需连接即可阅读；云同步、共享项目和目录访问需要连接。演奏者不能依赖场地 Wi-Fi，因此持有的乐谱是契约。
- **同步保留每位音乐家的标记。** 当库或项目分发到合奏时，每位音乐家的注释在合并中存活而非被覆盖——合奏标记在共享音乐上仍是个人化的。
- **记谱感知操作作用于文档，而非作为创作。** 此类产品中的移调、段落导航或 MusicXML/MIDI 导出源自存储的（或转换的）乐谱；阅读器的重心保持

definition.name: 3D Modeling Application
definition.overview:
A **3D Modeling Application** is used to create and edit three-dimensional geometry: the user builds objects in a 3D scene and directly shapes their form by manipulating the geometry's constituent elements, working on the model inside an interactive 3D view, and saving it as a reusable 3D asset.

The defining core is small:

```text
3D scene of positioned objects
└── directly editable geometry
    (create / edit shape and topology at the level of
     the geometry's elements — points, edges, faces, or equivalent)
    └── interactive 3D viewport as the working surface
        └── persistent model document (saved, reusable, exportable)
```

Everything else commonly associated with modern 3D software — primitive starters, modifier stacks, UV unwrapping, materials, sculpting modes, rendering, animation, asset marketplaces — is widespread in current products but is not what makes a product a 3D modeling application. Older modelers, NURBS-based and solid-based tools, and simplified architecture-oriented tools all satisfy the same core without most of those additions.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**3D建模应用程序**用于创建和编辑三维几何体：用户在3D场景中构建对象，并通过操作几何体的构成元素直接塑造其形态，在交互式3D视图内对模型进行工作，并将其保存为可复用的3D资产。

其定义性的核心很小：

```text
定位对象的3D场景
└── 可直接编辑的几何体
     （在几何体元素的层面创建/编辑形状和拓扑结构
     —— 点、边、面或等效元素）
     └── 作为工作表面的交互式3D视口
         └── 持久化模型文档（已保存、可复用、可导出）
```

现代3D软件通常关联的其他所有内容——基础图元起始、修改器堆栈、UV展开、材质、雕刻模式、渲染、动画、资产市场——在当前产品中很普遍，但这并不是使一个产品成为3D建模应用程序的原因。较旧的建模器、基于NURBS和基于实体的工具，以及简化的面向建筑的工具，都在没有这些大部分附加功能的情况下满足相同的核心。
definition.dc:
**3D scene.** The model lives in a shared three-dimensional space. Objects are placed in that space with position, rotation, and scale, and the scene is the container that holds all of them together. The scene is what gets saved as the working document.

**Editable geometry.** The center of the application is geometry that the user directly creates and changes. Crucially, the user works at the level of the geometry's constituent elements — its points, edges, and faces (or the equivalent control structures in curve- and solid-based modelers). Typical acts are drawing new edges, joining edges into faces, extruding faces into volume, splitting, merging, or erasing elements, and moving individual points to reshape a surface. This element-level directness is what distinguishes modeling from merely adjusting parameters or generating shapes from rules.

**Interactive 3D viewport.** Editing happens directly on the model inside a navigable 3D view — orbiting, panning, and zooming around the work while selecting and manipulating geometry in place. The viewport is both the primary working surface and the primary feedback surface: the user judges the shape by looking at it from different angles while editing it.

**Persistent model document.** The scene is saved as a file and can be reopened and continued. The model is also an asset: it can be exported in interchange formats and handed to renderers, game engines, animation tools, or 3D-printing pipelines. A modeling application whose output could not be saved or reused would not be a production tool.
definition.dc_zh:
**3D场景。** 模型存在于一个共享的三维空间中。对象在该空间中通过位置、旋转和缩放进行放置，场景是将所有对象容纳在一起的容器。场景作为工作文档被保存。

**可编辑几何体。** 应用的核心是用户直接创建和更改的几何体。关键是用户在几何体的构成元素级别上工作——其点、边和面（或基于曲线和实体的建模器中的等效控制结构）。典型操作包括绘制新边、将边连接成面、将面挤出成体积、分割、合并或擦除元素，以及移动单个点以重塑表面。这种元素级别的直接性是将建模与仅仅调整参数或根据规则生成形状区分开来的关键。

**交互式3D视口。** 编辑直接在可导航的3D视图中的模型上进行——围绕工作旋转、平移和缩放，同时就地选择和操作几何体。视口既是主要工作表面也是主要反馈表面：用户在编辑时从不同角度观察形状来判断。

**持久化模型文档。** 场景被保存为文件，可以重新打开并继续。模型也是一种资产：它可以以交换格式导出并传递给
definition.rules:
### Editing levels are explicit

The user chooses what level of the structure an operation targets — whole object, face, edge, or point. The same tool can behave differently at different levels, and selecting the wrong level is a common source of unexpected results. This object-vs-component distinction is a structural behavior of the Type, not a UI detail.

### Geometry must remain valid

Operations are constrained by the geometry's structure: an extrusion needs a face to pull from; cutting through a model requires the opposing face to be cleanly aligned; erasing an edge takes its adjacent face with it. Products guide or constrain the user (alignment aids, validity feedback) because invalid geometry breaks downstream use.

### Destructive vs non-destructive

Where non-destructive stacks exist, order matters: operations apply in sequence on top of the base geometry, and reordering changes the result. Where editing is destructive, undo/history is the safety net. Both postures exist in the market; the behavior difference is visible to the user.

### Precision is a first-class concern

Real-world scale matters — models are measured in actual units, and alignment/precision aids (snapping, inference, typed measurements) are central to the workflow, most deeply in architecture-oriented products.

### The viewport is the feedback loop

Shape judgments are made visually in 3D. Users constantly orbit around the model while editing, because a shape that looks right from one angle may be wrong from another.
definition.rules_zh:
### 编辑层级是明确的

用户选择操作针对结构的哪个层级——整个对象、面、边或点。同一工具在不同层级下可能表现不同，选择错误的层级是意外结果的常见来源。这种对象与组件的区别是该类型的结构行为，而非UI细节。

### 几何体必须保持有效

操作受几何体结构的约束：挤出需要一个面来拉取；切割模型需要对立面干净对齐；擦除一条边会带走其相邻的面。产品引导或约束用户（对齐辅助、有效性反馈），因为无效的几何体会破坏下游使用。

### 破坏性 vs 非破坏性

存在非破坏性堆栈的地方，顺序很重要：操作按顺序应用于基础几何体之上，重新排序会改变结果。在编辑是破坏性的地方，撤销/历史记录是安全网。市场上存在这两种姿态；行为差异对用户可见。

### 精度是一等关注点

实际世界尺度很重要——模型以实际单位测量，对齐/精度辅助（吸附、推断、类型化测量）是工作流程的核心，在面向建筑的产品中最为深入。

### 视口是反馈循环

形状判断在3D中视觉完成。用户在编辑时不断围绕模型旋转，因为从一个角度看正确的形状从另一个角度看可能是错误的。

definition.name: Digital Sculpting Application
definition.overview:
A **Digital Sculpting Application** is a 3D content-creation application in which the primary way of shaping a model is deforming a 3D surface directly with brush-like tools — the digital equivalent of working clay. Instead of building geometry from discrete components (extruding edges, editing vertices, assembling parametric features), the artist applies strokes to the surface to build up, carve, push, pull, smooth, and pinch material until the intended form emerges.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Persistent 3D surface (the model being shaped)
└── Brush-like tools applied along strokes on that surface
    │   (build up / remove / push / pull / smooth / pinch / move)
    └── Adjustable per stroke (size, strength, falloff, pressure)
        └── Shaped result kept as an exportable 3D model
```

Everything else commonly associated with modern sculpting products — subdivision levels, dynamic tessellation, voxel sculpting, symmetry, masking, sculpt layers, surface painting, retopology, baking, built-in renderers — is widely present in mature products but is not what makes an application a sculpting application. The vendors' own simplified and early-generation sculpting products (a single mesh, a small brush set, and an export button) are unmistakably members of this Type without any of those additions.

When the primary instrument shifts from brush strokes on a surface to component-level construction and parametric operations, the product belongs to the neighboring 3D Modeling Application Type; suite products legitimately offer both as separate modes.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**数字雕刻应用**是一种3D内容创作应用，其塑造模型的主要方式是通过类似画笔的工具直接对3D表面进行变形——这是数字化的粘土塑造过程。艺术家不是通过离散组件构建几何体（如拉伸边、编辑顶点、组装参数化特征），而是通过在表面上施加笔触来堆积、雕刻、推、拉、平滑和捏合材料，直到预期的形态显现。

其定义性结构很小：

```text
持久化的3D表面（正在塑造的模型）
└── 沿该表面笔触应用的类画笔工具
     │    （堆积 / 移除 / 推 / 拉 / 平滑 / 捏合 / 移动）
     └── 每笔触可调整（大小、强度、衰减、压力）
         └── 塑造结果保留为可导出的3D模型
```

现代雕刻产品通常关联的其他功能——细分级别、动态细分、体素雕刻、对称、遮罩、雕刻图层、表面绘制、重拓扑、烘焙、内置渲染器——在成熟产品中普遍存在，但这并非使应用成为雕刻应用的关键。厂商自身简化的早期世代雕刻产品（单一网格、少量画笔集和导出按钮）毫无疑问属于此类型，即使没有上述附加功能。

当主要工具从表面上的笔触转变为组件级构建和参数化操作时，该产品属于相邻的3D建模应用类型；套件产品可以合法地同时提供这两种作为独立模式。
definition.dc:
- **The sculpted surface** — a persistent 3D surface that embodies the model. In most products this is a polygon mesh; one major product offers a voxel alternative and can switch between the two, projecting edits across the switch. The surface is the single object every other capability acts upon.
- **Brushes as the primary instrument** — the application's central toolset is a palette of brushes, each a deformation operator applied along a stroke on the surface: build up material (clay-style), remove/carve, smooth, pinch, crease, inflate, flatten/planar, move/grab a region, stamp a shape. Most brushes have an inverse mode (subtract instead of add, unmask instead of mask).
- **Stroke control** — every stroke is governed by user-adjustable parameters: brush size/radius, strength/intensity, falloff, optional stamped shapes or alpha textures, and (typically) stylus pressure. These controls are what make the metaphor work: the same brush can block out a torso or engrave a wrinkle.
- **A persistent, exportable 3D model** — the sculpt lives in a native project and leaves the application as standard 3D geometry (or as geometry plus baked detail maps) for rendering, games, or printing.

If any of these is removed — no surface, no brush deformation, no persistent exportable model — the software is no longer a digital sculpting application.
definition.dc_zh:
雕刻表面 — 一个持久的3D表面，体现模型。在大多数产品中，这是一个多边形网格；一个主要产品提供体素替代方案，并可以在两者之间切换，跨切换投射编辑。表面是每个其他能力作用的单一对象。
画笔作为主要工具 — 应用程序的中心工具集是一个画笔调色板，每个画笔是一个沿着表面笔画应用的变形操作符：堆积材料（粘土风格）、移除/雕刻、平滑、捏合、褶皱、膨胀、展平/平面、移动/抓取区域、盖章形状。大多数画笔有反转模式（相减代替相加，取消遮罩代替遮罩）。
笔画控制 — 每个笔画由用户可调参数控制：画笔大小/半径、强度/强度、衰减、可选的盖章形状或Alpha纹理，以及（通常）手写笔压力。这些控制使隐喻工作：相同的画笔可以勾勒躯干或雕刻皱纹。
一个持久、可导出的3D模型 — 雕刻存在于本地项目中，并作为标准3D几何体（或几何体加烘焙细节贴图）离开应用程序，用于渲染、游戏或打印。
definition.rules:
- **Masked and hidden geometry is protected.** Brushes, paint, and (usually) topology operations do not affect masked or hidden regions; this is the standard way to sculpt in tight areas.
- **Resolution changes have consequences.** Operations that rebuild topology (remesh, dynamic tessellation, cutting tools) destroy stacked subdivision detail in products that use multires — vendors warn before it happens. Conversely, edits made at a coarse level project upward when returning to higher levels.
- **Inverse modes are systematic.** Nearly every brush has an opposite (add/subtract, mask/unmask, paint/erase); products expose it as a held or sticky toggle.
- **Cutting operations are camera-dependent.** Trim/split-style tools that cut through the model project from the camera; some products warn when the camera is in perspective because the near and far sides of the cut then differ.
- **Voxel/remesh operations expect closed geometry.** Voxel-based rebuilding resolves self-intersections and fills holes; open surfaces are closed automatically.
- **Export fidelity varies by format.** Sculpt-specific data (layers, face groups, vertex materials) survives only in formats that support it; the same product's export dialog documents the matrix. Plain formats carry geometry (and often vertex color) but drop sculpt structure.
- **No account or permission model.** Files and settings are local; there is no meaningful multi-user layer in this Type.
definition.rules_zh:
- **遮罩和隐藏几何体受到保护。** 画笔、绘制和（通常）拓扑操作不影响遮罩或隐藏区域；这是在狭窄区域进行雕刻的标准方式。
- **分辨率变化有后果。** 重建拓扑的操作（重新网格化、动态细分、切割工具）在使用多分辨率的产品中会破坏堆叠的细分细节——厂商会在发生前警告。相反，在粗粒度级别进行的编辑在返回更高级别时向上投影。
- **反向模式是系统性的。** 几乎每个画笔都有相反功能（添加/减去，遮罩/取消遮罩，绘制/擦除）；产品将其暴露为按住或粘性切换。
- **切割操作依赖于相机。** 穿过模型的修剪/分割式工具从相机投影；当相机处于透视模式时，某些产品会警告，因为切割的近侧和远侧会不同。
- **体素/重新网格化操作期望封闭几何体。** 基于体素的重建解决自相交并填充孔洞；开放表面会自动封闭。
- **导出保真度因格式而异。** 雕刻特定数据（图层、面组、顶点材质）仅在支持的格式中保留；同一产品的导出对话框记录了矩阵。普通格式携带几何体（通常还有顶点颜色）但丢弃雕刻结构。
- **无账户或权限模型。** 文件和设置是本地化的；此类型中没有有意义的多用户层。

definition.name: Procedural 3D Creation Application
definition.overview:
A **Procedural 3D Creation Application** creates 3D content by having the user author an explicit, persistent, editable rule structure — a network of connected operators, a parametric recipe, or code — which the application evaluates to produce 3D results (geometry and scene elements). When any part of the definition changes, the application regenerates the affected results automatically. The procedure, not the resulting geometry, is the artifact the user maintains and saves.

This is the Type's defining difference from neighboring 3D Types. In a direct-manipulation modeler, the user's persistent edits are made to the geometry itself, and the geometry is the document. Here the user's persistent edits are made to the rules from which geometry is derived — insert a step, rewire a connection, change a parameter, and the content recomputes. This makes the Type well suited to work where content must be revisable late in production, generated at scale (thousands of variations, vast scenes), and packaged into reusable tools.

The defining structure is small. Everything else commonly associated with procedural products — node-graph editors, specific data formats, simulation toolkits, real-time preview, USD pipelines — is standard capability or variant machinery, not the definition. Script-driven generation from earlier decades satisfies the same structure with no node graph at all.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**程序化3D创作应用**通过让用户编写显式的、持久的、可编辑的规则结构——即由相互连接的算子组成的网络、参数化配方或代码——来创建3D内容，应用评估该结构以生成3D结果（几何体与场景元素）。当定义的任意部分发生变化时，应用会自动重新生成受影响的结果。用户维护并保存的是该过程，而非生成的几何体。

这是该类型与邻近3D类型的根本区别。在直接操作建模器中，用户的持久性编辑直接作用于几何体本身，几何体即为文档。而在此处，用户的持久性编辑作用于生成几何体的规则——插入一个步骤、重新连接线路、更改参数，内容便会重新计算。这使得该类型非常适合那些需要在制作后期仍可修订内容、大规模生成（数千种变体、庞大场景）以及封装为可复用工具的工作场景。

其核心结构非常精简。通常与程序化产品相关联的其他一切——节点图编辑器、特定数据格式、模拟工具包、实时预览、USD管线——均为标准功能或变体机制，而非定义本身。早期几十年基于脚本的生成方式同样满足这一结构，且完全无需节点图。
definition.dc:
```text
Procedure (explicit, persistent, editable rule structure)
└── Evaluation (executing the procedure — some products call this "cooking")
    └── 3D data (geometry carrying attributes, scene elements)
        └── Regeneration: edits to the procedure propagate
            and recompute the affected results
```

Three properties held together, plus one domain binding. If any is removed, the product stops being this Type:

- **The procedure is the content of record.** The user authors and maintains an explicit rule structure — a wired graph of operators, a parametric definition, or code. The saved document is this definition. Without it, the product is a direct-manipulation modeler (geometry as the document) or a bare code library.
- **Evaluation produces the 3D results.** The application executes the definition to compute concrete 3D data and shows the evaluated results to the user. Without it, there is no 3D product — only a diagram or a text editor.
- **Regeneration on change.** Editing any part of the definition — inserting, reordering, rewiring, re-parameterizing — recomputes the affected output and propagates forward through the procedure, without the user re-authoring the result. Without it, the product is a one-shot generator or a static converter.
- **Primary output is 3D content.** The same authoring model aimed primarily at 2D output (textures, materials, image composites) belongs to the texture/material authoring and compositing Types.

The procedure can take several interchangeable forms inside one product: a visual network of nodes, per-parameter expressions and references between parameters, and embedded code. Mature products treat these as layers of the same underlying definition rather than as separate paradigms.
definition.dc_zh:
程序流程（显式、持久、可编辑的规则结构）
└── 执行评估（运行该流程——部分产品称之为“计算”）
    └── 三维数据（承载属性的几何体、场景元素）
        └── 重新生成：对程序流程的编辑会传播并重新计算受影响的结果
definition.rules:
- **The definition, not the result, is authoritative.** Editing geometry directly is either impossible, temporary, or an edit to a *specific evaluation* — the durable way to change content is to change the procedure. Products that permit sculpt-like direct edits typically do so as an operator stage inside the network.
- **Order in the procedure is meaning.** The same operators wired in a different order produce different results; reordering is a normal editing act, not a stylistic preference.
- **Evaluation is the cost center.** Every edit can trigger recomputation; mature products expose control over when this happens (continuously while dragging, on release, on demand) and over how expensive recomputation is managed, because a single parameter change can invalidate a large amount of computation.
- **Parameters are inputs, not annotations.** A parameter can be a static value, a computed expression, a reference to another parameter elsewhere, or a keyed animation. What looks like a simple number may be a live computation.
- **Changes propagate forward only.** Editing a node recomputes the nodes downstream of it; earlier parts of the network are unaffected. This one-way flow is what makes results reproducible.
- **Determinism is expected but managed.** Users expect the same definition to regenerate the same result; some products provide controls where performance optimizations could otherwise make results vary.
- **The tool boundary is the parameter interface.** Consumers of a packaged tool can only change what its author exposed — encapsulation is a user-facing rule, not just a convenience.
definition.rules_zh:
- **定义而非结果是权威依据。** 直接编辑几何体要么不可能，要么是临时的，要么是对*特定评估*的编辑——持久更改内容的唯一方式是更改过程。允许类似雕刻的直接编辑的产品，通常将其作为网络内的一个算子阶段来实现。
- **过程中的顺序具有意义。** 相同的算子以不同顺序连接会产生不同结果；重排是常规编辑操作，而非风格偏好。
- **评估是成本中心。** 每次编辑都可能触发重新计算；成熟产品提供对何时发生此过程（拖动时连续、释放时、按需）以及如何管理重新计算开销的控制，因为单个参数更改可能使大量计算失效。
- **参数是输入，而非注释。** 参数可以是静态值、计算表达式、对其他位置参数的引用，或关键帧动画。看似简单的数字可能是实时计算。
- **更改仅向前传播。** 编辑某个节点会重新计算其下游节点；网络的前序部分不受影响。这种单向流动确保了结果的可复现性。
- **确定性是预期但受管理的。** 用户期望相同定义重新生成相同结果；部分产品提供控制机制，以防性能优化导致结果差异。
- **工具边界即参数界面。** 封装工具的使用者只能更改其作者暴露的内容——封装是面向用户的规则，而不仅是便利措施。

definition.name: Rendering Management Application
definition.overview:
A **Rendering Management Application** is the logistics system for render workloads. It takes render jobs submitted from content-creation tools, holds them in a queue, schedules their frame-level work onto a pool of render machines, tracks every unit of work to completion, handles failures, and delivers the finished frames back to shared storage. The category is commonly known in the industry as a *render farm manager* or *render management system*.

Its defining core is small:

```text
Render job (the managed unit of record)
└── decomposed into frame-level executable units
    └── scheduled onto the render capacity estate
        (machines held as schedulable slots, grouped and qualified)
        └── dispatch-and-track loop
            (match → dispatch → track state → handle failure → close job)
```

The application itself does not compute images. The rendering is done by rendering applications and the studios' 3D/compositing software, which the manager launches on worker machines — vendors ship the two as separate products with separate documentation. When the primary job shifts to computing the images themselves, the product is a 3D Rendering Application; when it shifts to authoring the materials those images use, a Texture/Material Authoring Application; when the "jobs" are software builds from source control rather than render workloads, a Continuous Integration Platform.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**渲染管理应用程序**是渲染工作负载的物流系统。它接收来自内容创作工具提交的渲染任务，将其置于队列中，将帧级别的工作调度到一组渲染机器上，跟踪每个工作单元直至完成，处理故障，并将完成的帧交付回共享存储。该类别在行业中通常被称为*渲染农场管理器*或*渲染管理系统*。

其定义性的核心很小：

```text
渲染任务（被管理的记录单元）
└── 分解为帧级别的可执行单元
     └── 调度到渲染容量资源池
         （机器作为可调度槽位持有，进行分组和资格认证）
         └── 分发与跟踪循环
             （匹配 → 分发 → 跟踪状态 → 处理故障 → 关闭任务）
```

应用程序本身不计算图像。渲染由渲染应用程序和工作室的3D/合成软件完成，管理器在 worker 机器上启动这些软件——供应商将这两者作为独立产品并提供独立文档进行发布。当主要任务转向计算图像本身时，该产品即为3D渲染应用程序；当任务转向创作这些图像所使用的材质时，即为纹理/材质创作应用程序；当“任务”是来自版本控制的软件构建而非渲染工作负载时，即为持续集成平台。
definition.dc:
**The render job.** The unit of record is a persistent, identified job: what to run (a scene file or a command, together with the application that will execute it), over what span (a frame range or a parameterized task set), writing its output where, submitted by whom, at what priority. A job lives through a lifecycle — submitted, queued, executing, completed, failed, canceled — and accumulates its execution history (statuses, logs). Without the job as a managed record there is no management, only a row of machines.

**Decomposition into executable units.** A job is not dispatched as one lump. It is decomposed into small units — typically one per frame, sometimes chunks of frames or parameterized tasks — each of which can run independently on any suitable machine. This decomposition is what makes a render farm work: three hundred frames can render in parallel across three hundred slots, and one failed frame can be retried without redoing the other two hundred ninety-nine.

**The render capacity estate.** The machines are held as schedulable capacity. Each machine offers one or more execution slots; machines are grouped (pools, fleets, allocations, client groups) and qualified (tags, memory or GPU requirements, installed software, location) so that jobs can be matched to machines that can actually run them. The estate commonly mixes dedicated farm hardware with artist workstations and cloud instances.

**The dispatch-and-track loop.** A scheduler continuously matches pending job units to available slots under priority and policy, dispatches them, tracks each unit's state, captures its logs, handles failures (retry, requeue, kill), and closes the job when all of its units have completed. This loop is the application's central act; without it, a job list and a machine list are just two disconnected tables.

**The binding: content-production compute.** The workloads being managed are rendering jobs at the center — with compositing, simulation, transcoding, and similar command-driven content-production work as the standard extension — arriving from content-creation tools. The same scheduling skeleton, pointed at arbitrary batch computing with no DCC integration, frame anatomy, or render licensing, is a different software world (generic batch/HPC scheduling).
definition.dc_zh:
**渲染任务。** 记录单元是一个持久化、有唯一标识的任务：包含执行内容（场景文件或命令连同将要执行它的应用程序）、执行跨度（帧范围或参数化任务集）、输出位置、提交者及优先级。任务经历完整的生命周期——提交、排队、执行中、完成、失败、取消——并累积其执行历史（状态、日志）。没有作为受管记录的任务，就不存在管理，只是一排机器。

**分解为可执行单元。** 任务不会作为整体被分派，而是被分解为小单元——通常每个单元对应一帧，有时是帧块或参数化任务——每个单元都可以在任意合适的机器上独立运行。这种分解机制使渲染农场得以运作：三百帧可以并行渲染于三百个槽位中，而一帧失败时可单独重试，无需重新渲染其他二百九十九帧。

**渲染计算资源池。** 机器被视为可调度的计算资源。每台机器提供一个或多个执行槽位；机器按组划分（池、集群、分配组、客户端组）并按属性标记（标签、内存或GPU需求、已安装软件、物理位置），以便任务能匹配到可以实际执行它们的机器。资源池通常混合了专用农场硬件与艺术家工作站。
definition.rules:
### The manager launches renderers; it does not render

The defining division of labor: the manager decides *where and when*, the rendering application decides *how the pixels are made*. This is why the same manager can drive many different renderers and why vendors ship farm managers as separate products from their renderers.

### A job that cannot run waits visibly — it does not fail silently

If no machine satisfies a job's requirements, or a render license is unavailable, the job (or its units) stays in a waiting state, and the reason is surfaced — in the queue, or as an error in the unit's log. "Queued for lack of a suitable machine" is a normal, observable state, not an exception.

### Unit state aggregates upward

Job and sub-part statuses are derived from the state of their units: one running frame keeps the job "running"; one failed frame makes the job "failed" even while its siblings continue. This is why unit-level retry is the standard repair path — fixing one frame does not disturb the others.

### Shared storage is a precondition

Every machine that executes work must be able to read the scene and write the frames. Self-hosted products state this as an installation requirement; managed-cloud products replace it with file transfer into their own storage. A job whose files are unreachable fails on the worker, with the failure visible in its log.

### Workstation capacity belongs to its owner

Where artist workstations join the farm, the workstation's user controls when it may be used: rendering yields when the owner needs the machine — commonly automatically on user activity — and the owner can lock the machine explicitly or on a schedule. Jobs may be marked exempt from this courtesy for critical renders. A workstation's owner never loses the ability to evict render work from their own machine.

### Priority is relative, not absolute

Priority orders the queue; it does not guarantee resources. Per-user and per-project limits, license counts, and machine pools all modulate what a high priority actually obtains — which is why wrangler intervention (moving capacity between jobs) exists alongside priority as a control.

### Failure is expected and designed for

Frames fail: scenes crash, machines die, disks fill. The standard responses are unit-level retry, requeue after a fix, holding back machines that error repeatedly, and keeping logs close to every unit so the cause is findable. A farm manager that could not retry a single failed frame without re-rendering the job would not be usable.
definition.rules_zh:
### 管理器启动渲染器；它本身不渲染

定义性的分工：管理器决定*在哪里和何时*，渲染应用程序决定*像素如何生成*。这就是为什么同一个管理器可以驱动许多不同的渲染器，以及为什么供应商将农场管理器作为与其渲染器分离的产品发布。

### 无法运行的任务可见地等待——它不会静默失败

如果没有机器满足任务的需求，或者渲染许可证不可用，任务（或其单元）将保持在等待状态，并且原因会被呈现——在队列中，或作为单元日志中的错误。“因缺乏合适机器而排队”是一种正常的、可观察的状态，而不是异常。

### 单元状态向上聚合

任务和子部分的状态由其单元的状态推导：一个正在运行的帧使任务保持“运行中”；一个失败的帧使任务变为“失败”，即使其同级单元继续运行。这就是为什么单元级别的重试是标准的修复路径——修复一个帧不会干扰其他帧。

### 共享存储是先决条件

每台执行工作的机器都必须能够读取场景并写入帧。自托管产品将此作为安装要求陈述；托管云产品将其替换为文件传输到其自身存储。文件不可达的任务将在 worker 上失败，且失败在其日志中可见。

### 工作站容量属于其所有者

当艺术家工作站加入农场时，工作站的用户控制何时可以使用它：当所有者需要机器时渲染会让出——通常在用户活动时自动进行——并且所有者可以显式或按计划锁定机器。任务可以被标记为豁免此礼貌行为，用于关键渲染。工作站的所有者永远不会失去驱逐

definition.name: Texture / Material Authoring Application
definition.overview:
A **Texture / Material Authoring Application** creates the surface appearance of 3D models — texture maps and material definitions — and delivers that appearance as reusable assets into a 3D pipeline (game engines, renderers, and other 3D applications).

The defining core is small:

```text
Surface-appearance data (texture maps and/or material definitions)
  bound to 3D surface context the application itself holds
    → authored through editable, non-destructive structures
      → delivered as consumable appearance assets
```

Everything else the market associates with the category — PBR channel sets, layer stacks, node graphs, smart materials, mesh-map baking, UDIM tile scale, real-time ray-traced previews, AI texture generation — is widespread in current products but is not what makes the product this Type. Older pre-PBR texture painters and renderer-era procedural shading tools fit the same core without any of those specifics.

The Type sits in the 3D production pipeline between modeling (which delivers geometry) and rendering/engines (which consume appearance to produce images). Its deliverable is the **asset**, never the final image — that distinction is the boundary with 3D rendering software.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**纹理/材质创作应用**负责创建3D模型的表面外观——包括纹理贴图和材质定义——并将该外观作为可复用资产交付到3D管线中（游戏引擎、渲染器及其他3D应用）。

其定义性的核心非常精简：

```text
表面外观数据（纹理贴图和/或材质定义）
  绑定到应用自身持有的3D表面上下文
     → 通过可编辑、非破坏性的结构进行创作
       → 作为可消费的外观资产交付
```

市场将该类别关联的其他一切——PBR通道集、图层堆栈、节点图、智能材质、网格贴图烘焙、UDIM瓦片缩放、实时光线追踪预览、AI纹理生成——在当前产品中虽已普及，但并非使该产品成为此类型的本质特征。早期的PBR前纹理绘制工具和渲染器时代的程序化着色工具，即便不具备上述任何具体特性，也符合这一核心定义。

该类型位于3D生产管线中，介于建模（交付几何体）与渲染/引擎（消费外观以生成图像）之间。其交付物是**资产**，而非最终图像——这一区别构成了与3D渲染软件的边界。
definition.dc:
Three properties hold together. Remove any one and the product stops being this Type:

- **Surface-appearance data as the unit of record.** The product's central, persistent objects are texture maps and/or material definitions — data that describes how a 3D surface looks: its color, surface-normal detail, roughness or shininess, metalness, height, emissive glow, and similar qualities. The output is not geometry (that is modeling) and not an image (that is rendering); it is the appearance layer in between.
- **Binding to 3D surface context.** The application itself holds the 3D frame the appearance is authored against. In the painting form, that is an imported mesh with its UV layout, painted directly on the surface. In the procedural form, it is a material defined in surface terms — parameterized by UV space, surface position, and orientation — destined for 3D surfaces. The data model is surface-oriented, not a flat canvas. This is what separates the Type from raster image editing: an image editor used to paint a UV texture is image editing *serving* a texture pipeline, not a texture authoring application.
- **Delivery into the 3D pipeline.** The authored appearance leaves the application as consumable assets — exported texture-map sets (commonly organized and packed for a target engine or renderer) and/or reusable material definitions — to be applied to 3D models downstream. Without delivery, the product is a paint sandbox, not a production authoring tool.
definition.dc_zh:
定义核心：三个属性共同维系。移除任何一个，产品就不再属于此类型：

1. **表面外观数据作为记录单元。** 产品的核心持久对象是纹理贴图和/或材质定义——描述三维表面外观的数据：颜色、表面法线细节、粗糙度或光泽度、金属感、高度、自发光等。输出既不是几何体（建模），也不是图像（渲染），而是介于两者之间的外观层。
2. **绑定到三维表面上下文。** 应用程序本身持有外观创作所针对的三维框架。在绘制形式中，这是导入的网格及其UV布局，直接在表面上绘制。在程序化形式中，这是以表面术语定义的材质——通过UV空间、表面位置和方向参数化——旨在用于三维表面。数据模型是面向表面的，而非平面画布。这正是该类型与光栅图像编辑的区别：用于绘制UV纹理的图像编辑器是服务于纹理管道的图像编辑，而非纹理创作应用。
3. **交付到三维管道。** 创作的外观作为可消费资产离开应用程序——导出的纹理贴图集（通常为目标引擎或渲染器组织和打包）和/或可重用的材质定义——应用于下游的三维模型。
definition.rules:
- **Appearance is bound to surface coordinates.** The maps are meaningful only through the mesh's UV layout. If the UVs or mesh are modified in-product, the mesh must be exported together with the textures or the downstream application cannot map them correctly.
- **Authoring is non-destructive until export.** Layers, masks, and node parameters stay editable; the exported maps are a resolution of the stack at export time. Changing the stack and re-exporting is the normal iteration loop.
- **Channels follow the target workflow.** The set of maps a project carries matches the downstream shading model — a full PBR set for engine work, a reduced set for non-PBR targets. Products let the artist configure which channels exist and which layers affect them.
- **Mesh-driven effects adapt to the model.** Masks generated from curvature, occlusion, or position recompute against the mesh, so a weathering layer survives topology changes better than hand-painted masks.
- **Export must match the consumer.** Engines and renderers expect specific map naming, channel packing, bit depths, and color encodings; export presets exist because a correct-looking asset in the authoring tool can still arrive broken if delivered in the wrong arrangement.
- **The viewport is an instrument, not the deliverable.** Preview quality exists to validate the asset ("will this look right in the final render?"); the asset — maps and materials — is what leaves the application.
- **Baking transfers detail across meshes.** Normal/height/AO bakes move high-poly detail onto the low-poly mesh; baked maps then feed masks and generators rather than being painted from scratch.
definition.rules_zh:
- **外观绑定到表面坐标。** 贴图仅通过网格的UV布局才有意义。如果在产品内修改了UV或网格，必须将网格与纹理一起导出，否则下游应用无法正确映射它们。
- **创作在导出前是非破坏性的。** 图层、遮罩和节点参数保持可编辑；导出的贴图是导出时堆栈的解析结果。更改堆栈并重新导出是正常的迭代循环。
- **通道遵循目标工作流。** 项目携带的贴图集与下游着色模型相匹配——引擎工作使用完整的PBR集，非PBR目标使用精简集。产品允许艺术家配置哪些通道存在以及哪些图层影响它们。
- **网格驱动的效果适应模型。** 由曲率、遮挡或位置生成的遮罩会根据网格重新计算，因此风化图层比手绘遮罩更能承受拓扑变化。
- **导出必须匹配消费者。** 引擎和渲染器期望特定的贴图命名、通道打包、位深度和颜色编码；导出预设的存在是因为，在创作工具中看起来正确的资产，如果以错误的排列方式交付，到达时仍可能是损坏的。
- **视口是仪器，而非交付物。** 预览质量的存在是为了验证资产（“这在最终渲染中看起来对吗？”）；资产——贴图和材质——才是离开应用的内容。
- **烘焙在网格间转移细节。** 法线/高度/AO烘焙将高模细节转移到低模网格上；烘焙后的贴图随后馈送到遮罩和生成器中，而不是从头绘制。

definition.name: Interactive Prototype Builder
definition.overview:
An **Interactive Prototype Builder** is an application for building interactive simulations of a user interface. The author assembles a set of screens, connects them with user-defined interactions — "when the user taps this button, go to that screen" — and then experiences the result in a run mode that responds to input the way the intended product would.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Screen set (the staged UI surfaces)
└── Interactions (trigger → response, bound to elements or areas)
    └── Run mode (the simulation experienced without authoring tools)
        └── Design-artifact posture (a simulation of the product, not the product)
```

The prototype exists to make a design **experienceable, communicable, and testable** before engineering builds it: designers can preview flows, stakeholders can react to something concrete instead of static pictures, and researchers can put the intended product in front of real users. The boundary is equally important: a prototype simulates behavior with fabricated content and is never deployed as working software. When the artifact becomes a real application operating on real data, the work has left this Type.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**交互式原型构建器**是用于构建用户界面交互模拟的应用程序。作者组装一组屏幕，通过用户定义的交互将它们连接起来——“当用户点击此按钮时，跳转到那个屏幕”——然后在运行模式中体验结果，该模式会以预期产品的方式响应用户输入。

其定义性结构很小：

```text
屏幕集（分阶段的 UI 界面）
└── 交互（触发器 → 响应，绑定到元素或区域）
     └── 运行模式（无需使用创作工具即可体验的模拟）
         └── 设计产物姿态（产品的模拟，而非产品本身）
```

原型的存在是为了在工程团队构建之前，使设计变得**可体验、可沟通、可测试**：设计师可以预览流程，利益相关者可以对具体事物而非静态图片做出反应，研究人员可以将预期产品展示给真实用户。边界同样重要：原型使用虚构内容模拟行为，永远不会作为可用的软件部署。当产物变成在真实数据上运行的真实应用程序时，这项工作已离开此类型。
definition.dc:
**Screens.** The prototype is composed of one or more discrete UI surfaces — called frames, pages, or scenes depending on the product — that stage the simulated experience. Screens may be drawn with the tool's own design capabilities or imported as finished images; the Type does not require native drawing tools. Screens are the stages on which everything else happens.

**Interactions.** The author defines rules that bind a **trigger** — a user input event such as tap, click, hover, drag, or key press, occurring on a specific element or area of a screen — to a **response**: navigate to another screen, show or hide something, animate a change. The interaction is the unit that makes a mockup interactive; without it, the artifact is a static design.

**Run mode.** Every prototype builder provides a playback surface where the prototype runs as a simulation: the author or a viewer interacts with it, the current screen responds, transitions play, and navigation follows the defined interactions. The run mode is experienced without authoring tools — viewers navigate and trigger, but do not edit.

**Design-artifact posture.** The prototype stands in for the real product. Its data is fabricated, its buttons do not perform real transactions, and it is not deployed as software. This posture is what keeps the Type distinct from application builders.
definition.dc_zh:
**屏幕。** 原型由一个或多个离散的UI表面组成——根据产品不同，称为框架、页面或场景——这些表面模拟体验。屏幕可以用工具自身的绘图能力绘制或导入为成品图像；此类型不要求原生绘图工具。屏幕是其他一切发生的舞台。

**交互。** 作者定义规则，将**触发器**——用户输入事件，如点击、悬停、拖动或按键，发生在屏幕的特定元素或区域——绑定到**响应**：导航到另一个屏幕、显示或隐藏某些内容、动画变化。交互是使模型交互化的单位；没有它，工件是静态设计。

**运行模式。** 每个原型构建器提供一个播放表面，原型在此作为模拟运行：作者或查看者与之交互，当前屏幕响应，过渡播放，导航遵循定义的交互。运行模式在没有创作工具的情况下体验——查看者导航和触发，但不编辑。

**设计工件姿态。** 原型代表真实产品。其数据是伪造的，按钮不执行真实交易，并且不作为软件部署。这种姿态使此类型区别于应用构建器。
definition.rules:
- **Interactions bind to elements or areas, not to screens alone.** The same screen can behave differently depending on which part of it is triggered; a screen with no interactions is a dead end in the run mode.
- **The run mode is an experience, not an editor.** Viewers can navigate and trigger but cannot alter the prototype; editing happens only in the authoring surface, typically under separate permission.
- **Behavior is simulated.** Responses are pre-authored; data shown in the prototype is fabricated by the author. A prototype cannot do anything its interactions do not define.
- **Design and prototype stay coupled in same-file products.** Where the prototype is a mode of the design file, changes to a screen's visuals flow into the prototype automatically. Where screens are imported, the prototype reflects the imported snapshot; how design changes propagate afterward varies by product.
- **Multiple flows coexist in one prototype.** Each flow has its own starting screen; sharing can target the whole prototype or a single flow.
- **Fidelity is a spectrum under one interaction model.** The same trigger→response structure works over pencil-sketch photos, wireframes, and pixel-accurate screens; fidelity changes the look, not the mechanics.
definition.rules_zh:
- **交互绑定到元素或区域，而不仅仅是屏幕。** 同一屏幕可以根据触发的部分不同而表现不同；在运行模式中，没有交互的屏幕是一个死胡同。
- **运行模式是一种体验，而不是编辑器。** 查看者可以导航和触发，但不能更改原型；编辑仅在创作界面中进行，通常在单独的权限下。
- **行为是模拟的。** 响应是预先创作的；原型中显示的数据是由作者虚构的。原型不能做其交互未定义的任何事情。
- **在设计文件相同的产品中，设计和原型保持耦合。** 当原型是设计文件的一种模式时，对屏幕视觉的更改会自动流入原型。当屏幕被导入时，原型反映导入的快照；设计更改如何随后传播因产品而异。
- **多个流程在一个原型中共存。** 每个流程都有自己的起始屏幕；分享可以针对整个原型或单个流程。
- **保真度是一个在单一交互模型下的光谱。** 相同的触发器→响应结构适用于铅笔草图照片、线框图和像素精确的屏幕；保真度改变外观，而不是机制。

definition.name: UX Prototyping Application
definition.overview:
A **UX Prototyping Application** turns product ideas into experienceable interface simulations before any code is written: screens of the intended product are composed and linked with user-defined interactions into clickable flows, the simulation is run and shared, feedback and tests are collected, and the design is revised until it is approved for development.

The defining core is small:

```text
Screens of the intended interface
└── User-defined interactions (trigger → response)
    └── Clickable flows
        └── Run mode (the simulation, experienced without authoring tools)
            └── The validation loop: share → feedback/tests → iterate → approve → hand off
```

What makes this Type distinct is not an extra structure but the role the prototype plays: it is the instrument of the pre-implementation validation loop — the tool a team uses to decide *what to build* before building it. The prototype is never the deployed product; it operates on fabricated data and exists to be discussed, tested, and approved.

When the emphasis shifts to composing the polished screen design of record, the product is drifting toward a UI Design Application; when it shifts to the behavior depth and input realism of the simulation itself, toward an Interactive Prototype Builder; when the artifact becomes working software, the product has left prototyping entirely.
definition.overview_zh:
一款 **UX 原型设计应用** 在编写任何代码之前，将产品创意转化为可体验的界面模拟：将预期产品的界面组合并通过用户定义的交互链接成可点击的流程，运行并分享该模拟，收集反馈和测试，并修改设计直至其获得开发批准。

其定义性核心很小：

```text
预期界面的屏幕
└── 用户定义的交互（触发器 → 响应）
     └── 可点击的流程
         └── 运行模式（模拟体验，无需使用创作工具）
             └── 验证循环：分享 → 反馈/测试 → 迭代 → 批准 → 移交
```

使此类型独特的并非额外的结构，而是原型所扮演的角色：它是实施前验证循环的工具——团队在构建之前用来决定*构建什么*的工具。原型绝不是已部署的产品；它运行在虚构数据上，旨在被讨论、测试和批准。

当重点转向组合作为记录的精致界面设计时，产品正在向 UI 设计应用漂移；当重点转向模拟本身的行为深度和输入真实性时，则向交互式原型构建器漂移；当产物变成可工作的软件时，产品已完全离开原型设计领域。
definition.dc:
**Screens.** The prototype is composed of discrete UI surfaces — pages, screens, frames, or wireframes — each staging one state of the intended product. Screens are held in a navigable collection (a sitemap or page list) and may be drawn in the tool, assembled from UI element libraries, imported from design tools, or drafted by AI. Screens are the unit of composition and the targets of navigation.

**Interactions.** The behavior layer. The author binds a **trigger** — click/tap, double-click, hover, swipe, key press, page load, value change — on a screen element (or the screen itself) to a **response**: navigate to another screen, show/hide or toggle content, change an element's state, set a value. Interactions turn the screen set from pictures into an experience. Mature tools layer transitions and animations (easing, duration, delay) on top, and offer conditional logic — if-then-else rules over variables and input values — so the simulation can approximate real application behavior such as form validation.

**Flows.** Screens linked by interactions form paths through the product — a sign-up flow, a checkout flow. A prototype commonly carries multiple flows with their own starting points, and many tools also let the team *diagram* flows as first-class artifacts (user-flow maps, sitemaps) alongside the clickable simulation.

**Run mode.** A playback surface where the simulation responds to input the way the intended product would, experienced without authoring tools: a browser-based viewer, a full-screen present mode, or a companion app on a real device. The run mode is what stakeholders and test participants use; it is deliberately separate from the editor.

**The validation loop.** The prototype is built to leave the tool: shared by link with role-based access (viewers vs editors), annotated with comments, exercised in usability tests, revised through iterations or versions, and finally approved as the basis for development handoff. Mature tools make each stage of this loop a first-class surface — separate modes for experiencing, commenting, inspecting specs, and reading documentation.
definition.dc_zh:
**界面。** 原型由离散的UI表面组成——页面、屏幕、画框或线框图——每个表面展示产品的一个预期状态。界面被组织在一个可导航的集合（站点地图或页面列表）中，可以通过工具绘制、从UI元素库组装、从设计工具导入或由AI生成。界面是组合的基本单元和导航的目标。

**交互。** 行为层。创作者将**触发器**——点击/轻触、双击、悬停、滑动、按键、页面加载、值变更——绑定在界面元素（或界面本身）上，并指定**响应**：导航到另一个界面、显示/隐藏或切换内容、改变元素状态、设置值。交互将界面集合从静态图片转化为体验。成熟的工具在此基础上叠加转场动画（缓动曲线、时长、延迟），并提供条件逻辑——基于变量和输入值的if-then-else规则——使模拟能够接近真实应用行为，如表单验证。

**流程。** 由交互连接的界面形成了贯穿产品的路径——注册流程、结账流程。一个原型通常包含多个具有独立起点的流程，许多工具还支持将流程**绘制**为一等产物（用户流程图、站点地图），与可点击模拟并存。

definition.rules:
### The prototype is never the product

The simulation operates on fabricated data and is not connected to production systems. The moment the artifact is connected to a real backend and deployed as working software, the team has left prototyping — this is the Type's hard boundary. (A few current products deliberately blur it by generating runnable code from prototype intent; see Variants.)

### Interactions live on elements, and they can break

Interactions attach to screen elements or to the screen itself. When a targeted element or screen is deleted, the interaction becomes broken; mature tools flag these visibly so dead links don't reach stakeholders. Interactions can usually be copied between elements and screens.

### Visibility governs the simulation

Hidden screens and layers are excluded from the run mode and exports; what the stakeholder experiences is exactly what the author chose to expose. Preview access (sitemap, comments, specs) is typically configurable per share link.

### Viewers experience; editors change

The share model separates people who can navigate and comment on the simulation from people who can modify it. Approval flows on top of this: the prototype's link is the artifact being approved.

### The simulation is stateless between sessions

A prototype run starts from its defined starting screen(s); it carries no user accounts and no persisted user data. Conditional logic manipulates in-memory variables for the sake of realism, not record-keeping.

### Fidelity is a deliberate choice

Low-fidelity rendering is often a feature, not a limitation: sketchy screens keep feedback focused on structure and flow rather than visual polish. The same tool typically supports raising fidelity in place as the design matures.
definition.rules_zh:
### 原型绝不是产品

模拟运行在虚构数据上，且不连接到生产系统。一旦产物连接到真实后端并作为可工作的软件部署，团队就已离开原型设计——这是该类型的硬性边界。（少数当前产品通过从原型意图生成可运行代码来故意模糊它；参见变体。）

### 交互存在于元素上，且可能断裂

交互附加到屏幕元素或屏幕本身。当目标元素或屏幕被删除时，交互变得断裂；成熟的工具会明显标记这些，以便死链接不会到达利益相关者。交互通常可以在元素和屏幕之间复制。

### 可见性控制模拟

隐藏的屏幕和图层被排除在运行模式和导出之外；利益相关者体验的正是作者选择暴露的内容。预览访问（站点地图、评论、规格）通常可按分享链接配置。

### 查看者体验；编辑者修改

分享模型将可以导航和评论模拟的人与可以修改它的人分开。批准流程建立在此之上：原型的链接是被批准的产物。

### 模拟在会话之间是无状态的

原型运行从其定义的起始屏幕开始；它不携带用户账户，也不持久化用户数据。条件逻辑操作内存中的变量以追求真实感，而非记录保存。

### 保真度是刻意选择

低保真度渲染通常是一个功能，而非限制：草图般的屏幕使反馈集中在结构和流程上，而非视觉精致度。同一工具通常支持随着设计成熟而就地提高保真度。

definition.name: Interactive Web Design Application
definition.overview:
An **Interactive Web Design Application** is a designer-facing visual application for designing interactive web experiences: experiences whose motion and behavior — what happens when a visitor clicks, hovers, scrolls, or when a page loads — are designed as part of the design itself, on a visual canvas, and published as a live web artifact.

The defining core is small:

```text
Visual canvas composing the web experience
└── Authored behavior (trigger → animated / state response)
    └── Live published web artifact
        (a hosted site, or an interactive experience embedded in a web page)
```

Each part is load-bearing:

- without the **visual canvas**, the work becomes code-first web development rather than a designer-facing design application;
- without **authored behavior**, the product is a static design tool or a plain website builder;
- without the **live published artifact**, the product is a prototyping or mockup tool — the design would be a specification handed to developers rather than the deliverable itself.

The market expresses this Type through two delivery poles. In the **full-site pole**, the entire website is designed and hosted in the application. In the **interactive-content pole**, the application produces self-contained interactive experiences that are embedded into web pages owned by other systems. Both poles publish a live web artifact; the design activity is the same.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**交互式网页设计应用**是面向设计师的可视化应用，用于设计交互式网页体验：这些体验中的动态与行为——即访客点击、悬停、滚动或页面加载时发生的变化——作为设计本身的一部分，在可视化画布上进行设计，并发布为实时的网页产物。

其定义性核心很小：

```text
在可视化画布上组合网页体验
└── 创作行为（触发器 → 动画/状态响应）
     └── 实时发布的网页产物
         （托管站点，或嵌入网页中的交互式体验）
```

每个部分都至关重要：

- 没有**可视化画布**，工作就变成了代码优先的网页开发，而非面向设计师的设计应用；
- 没有**创作行为**，该产品就是一个静态设计工具或普通的网站构建器；
- 没有**实时发布的产物**，该产品就是一个原型或模型工具——设计将作为规格说明交给开发人员，而非交付物本身。

市场通过两个交付极点来表达这种类型。在**整站极点**，整个网站在应用内设计和托管。在**交互式内容极点**，应用生成自包含的交互式体验，嵌入到其他系统拥有的网页中。两个极点都发布实时网页产物；设计活动是相同的。
definition.dc:
**1. The canvas composition.** The designer works on a visual canvas where a project contains pages or screens, and each page is composed of directly manipulated elements — text, images, shapes, media, and in some products 3D objects. The composition is persistent and re-openable: elements remain individually editable objects, never flattened output. Layout is freeform rather than section- or template-constrained, which is what allows expressive, non-standard experiences.

**2. Authored behavior.** The designer selects an element and composes what it *does*: a trigger (click, hover, scroll position or progress, page load, timer) and a response (animated property changes such as position, opacity, scale, or rotation; state changes; multi-step sequences). This behavior layer is authored in the same tool and lives inside the same artifact as the layout. It is design material, not an afterthought and not a developer hand-off.

**3. The live web artifact.** Publishing produces a functioning web experience — a hosted website, or an interactive experience embedded into a web page — reachable by the end audience in a browser. There is no prototype-to-development stage: the design is the deliverable, and edits to the design flow into the live artifact.

One structure, many implementations:

```text
Concept:         The canvas
Implementations: CSS-grade visual designer, freeform design studio,
                 free-roaming pixel canvas, 3D scene editor

Concept:         Authored behavior
Implementations: timeline animation sequencer, state + event system,
                 trigger/sequence panels, reusable interaction presets

Concept:         The live web artifact
Implementations: platform hosting with custom domains, HTML/CSS export,
                 embeddable web components / embed codes,
                 webhook publishing into an external CMS
```

A reader who has only seen one pole should still recognize the other: a hosted animated brand site and an interactive report embedded inside a corporate CMS are the same Type with different delivery.
definition.dc_zh:
1. 画布构图。设计师在一个视觉画布上工作，其中项目包含页面或屏幕，每个页面由直接操纵的元素组成——文本、图像、形状、媒体，在某些产品中还有3D对象。构图是持久且可重新打开的：元素始终保持为可单独编辑的对象，从不扁平化输出。布局是自由形式的，而不是受部分或模板限制，这允许表达性、非标准的体验。

2. 编排行为。设计师选择一个元素并组合其*作用*：一个触发器（点击、悬停、滚动位置或进度、页面加载、计时器）和一个响应（动画属性变化，如位置、透明度、缩放或旋转；状态变化；多步骤序列）。这个行为层在同一个工具中编排，并位于与布局相同的工件中。它是设计材料，而不是事后想法或开发者移交。

3. 实时网络工件。发布产生一个功能性的网络体验——一个托管的网站，或嵌入到网页中的交互式体验——最终用户可以通过浏览器访问。没有原型到开发的阶段：设计就是交付物，对设计的编辑会流入实时工件。
definition.rules:
- **Behavior lives inside the published artifact.** By default there is no development hand-off; the designed behavior ships with the design. Code extends rather than replaces this (code embeds, custom events, export in some products).
- **Preview precedes publish; publish updates the live artifact.** Interaction design is judged at runtime — how it looks and how it responds — so previewing behavior before release is a first-class step. Version history or backups are common at mature products.
- **Interactions respond to viewer input at runtime.** The artifact is computed live in the visitor's browser; motion can be adapted for accessibility (reduced-motion support exists in some products).
- **Embed delivery is deliberately isolated.** In the content pole, the experience runs inside a page the application does not own; the point is that the host's CMS, analytics, and infrastructure remain untouched while the interactive layer is added.
- **Content and design are separable but distinct.** Where content bindings exist, editors change content without touching designed layout or behavior; the designed interaction remains stable across content updates.
- **Commerce, site operations, and large-scale content workflows are not part of the Type.** They belong to site builders, CMSs, and neighboring applications; this Type may coexist with them via embeds or integrations.
definition.rules_zh:
- **行为存在于发布的产物内部。** 默认情况下没有开发交接；设计的行为随设计一起发布。代码扩展而非替代这一点（在某些产品中代码嵌入、自定义事件、导出）。
- **预览先于发布；发布更新实时产物。** 交互设计在运行时被评判——它的外观和响应方式——因此在发布前预览行为是一等步骤。在成熟产品中，版本历史或备份很常见。
- **交互在运行时响应查看者输入。** 产物在访客的浏览器中实时计算；运动可以为无障碍性进行适应（某些产品中存在减少运动支持）。
- **嵌入交付是刻意隔离的。** 在内容极点，体验在应用不拥有的页面内运行；重点在于在添加交互层的同时，宿主的 CMS、分析和基础设施保持未受触动。
- **内容和设计可分离但不同。** 在存在内容绑定的地方，编辑者更改内容而不触及设计的布局或行为；设计的交互在内容更新中保持稳定。
- **商务、站点运营和大规模内容工作流不属于此类型。** 它们属于站点构建器、CMS 和邻近应用；此类型可通过嵌入或集成与它们共存。

definition.name: Landing Page Builder
definition.overview:
A **Landing Page Builder** is a marketing-side application for creating, publishing, and managing standalone web pages whose single job is to convert incoming campaign traffic — a visitor who "lands" on the page from an ad, email, or social post completes one desired action: submitting a form, signing up, buying, or clicking through.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Standalone campaign page (unit of record)
└── built to drive one conversion goal (call to action)
    └── assembled visually, without writing code
        └── published to a live web address
```

Three properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a landing page builder:

- **The standalone campaign page as the unit of record** — a persistent, individually managed single-purpose page. Not a fragment embedded in pages owned by other systems, and not one page of a navigable multi-page site. Landing pages typically do not link into a site's homepage navigation; they exist apart from it, paired with a specific campaign.
- **Visual no-code construction** — the page is assembled by direct visual manipulation: dragging elements and sections onto a canvas, starting from a professionally designed template. Writing code is not the primary building act.
- **Publication to a live web address** — the built page becomes a functioning page reachable at a URL, hosted by the product or published through a provided path, usually on the marketer's own domain or a product subdomain.

The binding purpose across all three is conversion: the page exists to turn campaign visitors into leads or customers. Remove that purpose and the artifact is just a web page.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**落地页构建器**是营销侧的应用程序，用于创建、发布和管理独立的网页，这些页面的唯一任务是将传入的活动流量转化为行动——从广告、电子邮件或社交帖子“着陆”到该页面的访客完成一个期望的动作：提交表单、注册、购买或点击跳转。

其定义性结构很小：

```text
独立的活动页面（记录单元）
└── 旨在驱动一个转化目标（行动号召）
     └── 通过可视化方式组装，无需编写代码
         └── 发布到实时的网络地址
```

三个属性。如果移除其中任何一个，该产品就不再可被识别为落地页构建器：

- **以独立的活动页面作为记录单元** —— 一个持久化、单独管理的单一用途页面。它不是嵌入在其他系统拥有的页面中的片段，也不是可导航的多页面网站中的一页。落地页通常不链接到网站的主页导航中；它们独立于网站存在，并与特定的营销活动配对。
- **可视化无代码构建** —— 页面通过直接的视觉操作进行组装：将元素和区块拖放到画布上，从专业设计的模板开始。编写代码不是主要的构建行为。
- **发布到实时的网络地址** —— 构建好的页面成为可在 URL 处访问的功能性页面，由产品托管或通过提供的路径发布，通常位于营销人员的自有域名或产品子域名上。

贯穿这三者的核心目的是转化：页面的存在是为了将活动访客转化为潜在客户或客户。移除这一目的，该产物就只是一个普通的网页。
definition.dc:
```text
Campaign
└── Landing Page (unit of record)
    ├── Page content: sections / elements / copy
    ├── Conversion goal: the call to action (form, button, purchase, click-through)
    └── Published address (custom domain or product subdomain)
```

- **Landing page** — the central object. A standalone page with its own content, its own settings, and its own published address. Products hold pages in a list where each page can be edited, previewed, published, unpublished, duplicated, and grouped (by campaign, client, or purpose).
- **Call to action (CTA)** — the conversion goal the page is built around. It may be a form, a button, a purchase, or a click to another destination. The CTA is what distinguishes a landing page from a general web page: everything on the page exists to serve it.
- **Page content** — the sections and elements the marketer arranges: headlines, text, images, video, forms, buttons. Assembly is visual; the editor is the primary workspace.
definition.dc_zh:
营销活动
└── 着陆页（基本单元）
    ├── 页面内容：部分/元素/文案
    ├── 转化目标：行动号召（表单、按钮、购买、点击通过）
    └── 发布地址（自定义域名或产品子域名）
definition.rules:
- **The page is independent of any site.** A landing page has its own address and lifecycle; it is published, edited, and retired on its own, not as part of a site structure.
- **One page, one goal.** The product's design guidance and structure push toward a single call to action; the page is evaluated by one conversion metric.
- **Publishing is explicit and reversible.** Edits do not go live until published; a live page can be unpublished without being destroyed.
- **Leads are captured, not managed.** The system of record for the lead relationship is elsewhere (CRM/email); the builder stores the capture and hands it off.
- **Internal traffic can distort measurement.** Some products let account admins filter internal IP addresses so team visits do not count as conversions.
- **Access control appears at team/agency scale.** Products serving agencies provide user roles and client-level segmentation; a solo marketer may never encounter them.
definition.rules_zh:
- **页面独立于任何网站。** 落地页拥有自己的地址和生命周期；它独立发布、编辑和退役，而非作为网站结构的一部分。
- **一页一目标。** 产品的设计指导和结构推动单一的行动号召；页面通过一个转化指标进行评估。
- **发布是显式且可逆的。** 编辑在发布前不会上线；已上线的页面可以取消发布而不会被销毁。
- **捕获潜在客户，而非管理。** 潜在客户关系的记录系统在其他地方（CRM/电子邮件）；构建器存储捕获内容并移交。
- **内部流量可能扭曲测量。** 某些产品允许账户管理员过滤内部 IP 地址，以便团队访问不计入转化。
- **访问控制在团队/代理机构规模出现。** 服务代理机构的产品提供用户角色和客户级细分；独立营销人员可能永远不会遇到这些功能。

definition.name: Visual Website Builder
definition.overview:
A **Visual Website Builder** is a no-code site-creation application: it lets a person assemble a complete website — its pages, sections, content, and appearance — through direct visual manipulation in a purpose-built editor, and publish it as a functioning website at a web address, without writing code as the primary building act.

The defining structure is small:

```text
The Site (a whole web presence — one or more pages)
└── composed of arranged sections/elements carrying content
    └── assembled and continuously re-edited visually, without code
        └── published as a live functioning website at a web address
```

Three properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a visual website builder:

- **Visual no-code assembly** — the building act is direct manipulation of pages, sections, and elements in an editor. Without it, the product is a code-first web development tool.
- **The whole website as the unit of work** — the artifact is a whole web presence, not a single campaign page and not a fragment embedded in pages owned by other systems. Without it, the product is a landing page builder or an embedded-content tool.
- **The published live website as the deliverable** — the assembled artifact becomes a functioning website reachable at a web address, with the product providing the path to publication. Without it, the product is a design tool or an unpublished prototype.

Everything commonly associated with modern builders — template libraries, drag-and-drop as a specific gesture, responsive machinery, AI site generation, commerce, blogging, CMS, app marketplaces, contributor roles — is widespread in current products but is not part of the defining core. Hosted page-builder ancestry, desktop publish-to-host builders, and Flash-era site builders all fit this definition without any of those specifics.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**可视化网站构建器**是一种无代码网站创建应用程序：它允许用户通过专用编辑器中的直接视觉操作来组装完整的网站——包括其页面、区块、内容和外观——并将其发布为在特定网络地址上运行的功能网站，而无需将编写代码作为主要的构建行为。

其定义性结构很小：

```text
网站（一个完整的网络存在——一个或多个页面）
└── 由承载内容的排列区块/元素组成
     └── 通过视觉方式组装并持续重新编辑，无需代码
         └── 发布为在特定网络地址上运行的实时功能网站
```

三个属性。如果移除其中任何一个，该产品就不再可被识别为可视化网站构建器：

- **可视化无代码组装** — 构建行为是在编辑器中对页面、区块和元素进行直接操作。如果没有这一点，该产品就是一个代码优先的网页开发工具。

### Edits and the live site are separated by publish

Work accumulates as a draft; visitors see the last published state. Saved changes do not appear on the live site until publish. This separation — draft vs live — is the central state rule of the Type.

### The live site remains editable

Publication is not an end state. The site can be reopened and edited at any time after publishing; changes go live on the next publish. Unpublishing takes the site offline while preserving the artifact.

### Concurrent editing is commonly constrained

Some products constrain simultaneous editing of the same site — parallel edits from multiple sessions risk overwriting each other. Real-time multi-user editing exists in the professional pole but is not universal; contributor roles commonly gate who may edit what.

### Structure constrains placement

The editing model defines where units may be placed. Structured editors distinguish freely-editable areas from structured areas (e.g., collection or gallery sections that render their own content) — blocks cannot be added everywhere. Free-canvas editors constrain differently (absolute placement rather than flow layout). The rule is product-specific in form but structural in kind: the editor's layout model governs what placements are legal.

### The editor is an online application (dominant implementation)

In the dominant hosted shape, the editor requires a connection to the platform; work cannot proceed offline, and the site's files are not handled as local documents. Desktop/export lineages relax this, at the cost of operating hosting themselves.

### Version history protects the artifact

Publishing repeatedly does not destroy prior states; products retain site history so a previous version can be restored. This is the safety net that makes continuous live editing safe.
